text.brief: On May 14, 1995, the Dalai Lama named six-year-old Gedhun Choekyi Nyima the eleventh Panchen Lama.
text.record: Security forces took the boy and his parents into custody within days. The Party jailed Chadrel Rinpoche, the abbot who led the search. In November it staged a lottery with a golden urn and installed its own candidate, Gyaincain Norbu. Gedhun has not appeared in public since 1995. In 2020 Congress passed the Tibetan Policy and Support Act, which states that the choice of the next Dalai Lama belongs to Tibetan Buddhists alone.
text.reading: The Party took a child to control a succession decades away, so Time became the weapon. It borrowed a Qing court urn to dress a political choice as a religious rite, which is Stratagem 14.
text.gapText: Architecture Principles. The defender voiced concern for twenty-five years before it wrote the principle of religious succession into law.
text.fix: Name the officials who hold a disappeared person and apply the sanctions the law already allows, year after year.
